hero.h1: In service to the soil that sustains us all
hero.intro: The Soil Food Web Foundation is a nonprofit organization carrying forward the life’s work of Dr. Elaine Ingham, empowering communities everywhere to restore and protect the Earth’s soil and living systems.

missionVision.mission: To honor and grow Dr. Elaine Ingham’s legacy of empowering communities to restore and protect the Earth’s soil and living systems, by sharing teaching and learning about the soil food web, pursuing knowledge related to soil, plant, and planetary health, incubating regenerative agricultural and ecosystem practices, and building community and financial support for soil food web teaching, research, and practice.
missionVision.vision: Healthy, living soil in every terrestrial ecoregion on the planet, nurtured by local communities who understand why soil health is the foundation of ecosystem, agricultural, planetary, and human wellbeing.

history.h2: Rooted in legacy, growing in impact

entries.title: Ph.D., Colorado State University
entries.body: Elaine Ingham earns her Ph.D. in soil microbiology at Colorado State University, following a B.A., cum laude, from St. Olaf College (1974) and an M.S. in microbiology from Texas A&M University. Her first scientific papers appear in 1982, beginning with work on ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence of mycorrhizal root infections.

entries.title: The foundational paper
entries.body: She co-authors “Interactions of Bacteria, Fungi, and their Nematode Grazers: Effects on Nutrient Cycling and Plant Growth” (Ecological Monographs 55:119–140), detailing the relationships between soil food web trophic groups and their role in plant nutrition.

entries.title: Research and teaching
entries.body: Postdoctoral research at the University of Georgia’s Institute of Ecology, then the faculty of Oregon State University (1986 to 2002) as Instructor and Associate Professor. She serves as the first President of the Soil Ecology Society, as Program Chair of the Ecological Society of America, and co-authors the USDA’s Soil Biology Primer (1999). Across her career: 89 publications, among them 53 journal articles, nine book chapters and thirteen technical reports.
entries.note: Copy deck v2 section 3.2 dates the Oregon State University post 1986 to 2002; this entry runs 1985 to 2002 because it also covers the Georgia postdoc. Confirm the start year against Dr. Ingham's CV before publish.

entries.title: Soil Foodweb Inc.
entries.body: She founds Soil Foodweb Inc., bringing microscopy-based soil assessment to growers.

whatWeDo.h2: Four ways we grow this work

pillars.title: Teaching & Learning
pillars.body: World-class education in soil biology, from foundation courses to professional certification, with workshops in a growing list of ecoregions and support that makes learning accessible.

pillars.title: Pursuing Knowledge
pillars.body: Replicating key experiments, opening our trial and case-study data, and advancing microscopy and lab methods, so more people understand why the soil food web works.

pillars.title: Incubating Applied Practice
pillars.body: Ecoregion hubs that integrate education, composting, microscopy, and consulting; partnerships with farmers to trial and document soil food web practices where they live.

pillars.title: Building Community & Support
pillars.body: A global network of students, volunteers, donors, and advisors who make this mission durable, and welcoming to newcomers.

elaine.h2: The woman who started it all
body: Dr. Elaine Ingham pioneered research in soil biology, expanding the world’s knowledge of living soil, and made her science radically accessible, so that anyone, anywhere, could learn to restore the soil beneath their feet.
This Foundation is her living legacy, and we hold it with care: not by asking the world to take her word for it, but by opening her science and expanding our community of practice.
